A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LayerTracer, with matching methods, experiments and identifiable figures and tables. All material is readable, including v2's supplementary Appendices A–C. v1 ends after its references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and vectorization experiments, quantitative comparisons, a serpentine-layout ablation and a user study with 46 participants.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds gradient-colored generation examples, supplementary outputs and failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 5 add a gradient-capable variant using gradient-colored training samples and the cited gradient-layer vectorization method. The core DiT, LoRA, image conditioning, loss and differential vectorization pipeline remain unchanged. Newly disclosed per-style LoRA training does not establish an architectural revision.

E1.justification: v2 adds a demonstrated gradient-filled SVG generation scenario and associated training examples. LayerSVG, Noto-Emoji, the existing icon/emoji/illustration coverage and the two main tasks remain. Supplementary examples and newly disclosed category counts do not establish additional domains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Vecfusion/VectorFusion, SVGDreamer and DiffSketcher for generation, and Diffvg, LIVE and O&R for vectorization. The user-study comparators also remain unchanged. The newly cited gradient vectorizer is used as a component, not evaluated as an additional baseline.

E3.justification: The shared benchmark sizes and stated training budgets remain unchanged. However, v2 Appendix A and Figure 10 ask which vectorization preserves the original image's characteristics, whereas both main texts describe judging logical layering. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a changed evaluation criterion or inconsistent documentation of the retained study.

E4.justification: Appendix C and Figure 13 add qualitative failure analysis covering repetition, incorrect layering and inconsistencies between frames in the full method. The existing serpentine-layout ablation is retained; no new quantitative robustness or sensitivity study is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The user-study proportions are retained; the newly disclosed questionnaire size is procedural information, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises the Full model's test MSE from 1.99 × 10^-4 to 1.96 × 10^-4, without establishing a rerun. Tables 1–2 and the user-study chart retain their results. Figures 5, 11 and 13 add gradient outputs, further generation examples and qualitative failures.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), covering positional encoding, attention, LoRA and conditional flow matching, remain mathematically equivalent. The explanatory edits introduce no new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about cognitive-aligned SVG synthesis, unified generation/vectorization, the process-centric dataset and superior quality/editability. The gradient demonstration does not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C explicitly acknowledges failures of the full method and distinguishes repetition that adjacent-frame deduplication can mitigate from incorrect layering and frame inconsistencies that damage output quality. This adds concrete qualifications beyond the unchanged general limitations in Section 5.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: learning rate 0.001, separate style-specific LoRAs, 3K/2K/15K training counts, A100 80GB hardware and default baseline settings. Appendices A–B additionally disclose questionnaire structure, data sources, designer layer reorganization, filtering and Florence-2 captioning. These are newly documented details, not evidence that the retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on controllable DiTs, including MakeAnything, DiffDecompose and EasyControl, plus references supporting gradient vectorization and Florence-2 captioning. This extends the cited context without substantially changing the paper's positioning against optimization-based and direct SVG generation methods.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the opening explanation, makes localized terminology and wording edits, removes ACM boilerplate and placeholder author headers, and adds acknowledgements and supplementary sections. The main section order and most of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the ACM presentation with a different template, changing typography, headings and figure/table placement throughout. It adds the gradient figure and four supplementary figures while retaining and relocating the original displays. Table 1 also corrects the CLIP-Score direction arrow from downward to upward.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added training, dataset and survey documentation makes the work easier to reproduce and assess, while concrete failure cases improve transparency about its limitations. These support a modest overall gain. The appendix's image-fidelity question conflicts with the main text's layering-rationality interpretation, leaving that part of the evidence unclear.
